reason: Researched hold, not a default one. The defensive risk-premia book is +4.32% vs SPY +2.94% with a -2.39% max drawdown, and this week's work confirms each leg rather than challenging it: UNH (+6.3% on the leg) beat Q3 on Oct 13 and raised FY adjusted EPS guidance to at least $20.50 with the medical cost ratio down to 88.4%; BRK-B (+6.0%) closed at a 3-month high on Friday as money left tech; TLT (-1.75%, -8% stop well away at ~74.95) is recovering as the 10-year eased from a 5.31% 24-year high to 5.10%, which is the term-premium sleeve doing its job; GLD (-4.1%) is 24% below its January record because real yields are at multi-decade highs, which is precisely the contrarian-value entry the mandate describes, so I hold it without chasing. SVXY (-2.4%) is the leg I looked at hardest: VIX closed 19.99 on 10-16, up from 15 a week earlier, with ~50% CME odds of a second Fed hike on Oct 28 and an AI-bubble scare running, so a further vol spike is plausible; but a higher VIX also means a richer volatility-risk premium to harvest, the leg is only 4% with a -20% stop (max 0.8% of NAV), and I would rather let the stop decide than churn it at a 7-week low. The EWZ sleeve took profit at +12.9% on Oct 5 after the first round; the Oct 25 runoff is a technical tie (Datafolha 46/44, BTG tie) and EWZ is already +11.6% on the month, so re-entering a binary event into strength is the opposite of mean-reversion, and the 7% stays in cash at 4% - 46% cash is appropriate with the Fed meeting and a Hormuz-driven $101 oil price inside the next two weeks. I considered adding to gold or buying energy, but energy is momentum, not contrarian, and belongs in my Round 2 book (where I just put it), and adding gold now would be averaging into a position already sized at 10%. Holding costs nothing; replacing legs would cost basis points for no identified edge. Novelty rule: zero symbol overlap with my Round 2 book.
